title: The maker of the game Rad Cohesion tests its multiplayer against a headless agent, and posts the scores
summary: @oscillatory.net (274 followers) is making Rad Cohesion, a game in which pieces are placed on a polyhedron-shaped board to complete and clear its faces. On Sat 14 Nov 20:19Z: "testing rad cohesion multiplayer with a headless agent", with a screenshot of a "Multiplayer score race" page. At 00:07Z on Sun 15 Nov: "was able to feel smug for handily beating the first two versions, but by v3 i'm just getting fully rolled", with a scoreboard (alt text: Agent1 638700, Player1 · you 27100). At 02:46Z: "just gotta slow em down a bit by introducing a 3 second pause after each piece placement", saying the agent "greedily tries to complete single faces"; the new scoreboard reads Me: 30,300, Agents: 18,600, 18,400, 16,600. A last reply: "i also have cope that humans are superior if given just the graphical view, but admittely haven't run the experiment with a large multimodal model". The four posts have 3, 0, 0 and 0 likes.

sensitive: Small account, very low engagement (0 to 3 likes): R7, hero only, and a reviewer should ask whether the attention would be welcome. The account's later post announcing that multiplayer is live, and a video of play, quote their own Fri 13 Nov post and sit in flagged story 28 (jokey mental-health word, R10); they are left out. "cope" and "getting fully rolled" are the author's own words about themself.
